b6d8f9da3047891c179408bf937652d24d430b40.summary: IBM X-Force researchers report that Zeus Sphinx, a commercially sold banking Trojan that emerged in August 2015 against UK banks, has been found in Brazil. The Brazilian variant, Sphinx v2, targets online banking and Boleto payment services at three top Brazilian banks and one Colombian bank. It uses real-time webinjections to collect PINs and personal data, and can reroute Boleto payments to the criminal by generating altered barcodes. The malware is sold on underground forums. The researchers say the Brazilian version most likely comes from the same developer and that more variants may…

b61e4c6ba0bf6f9658599075cdee2c82a340f909.summary: Ransom-ISAC, working with Bridewell, analyses the command-and-control infrastructure behind a September 2025 cryptocurrency and data theft intrusion that targeted developers through a weaponised private GitHub repository. Servers are clustered by fingerprints such as the EmbedIO web server, a shared RDP certificate name and hosting networks. The report links some indicators to a May 2025 NPM supply-chain campaign described by Aikido. It assesses with low to medium confidence that two cooperating actors were involved, possibly a DPRK-linked group and Russia-facing pre-attack infrastructure,…
